title: Informal Conjecture (constant-size M)
statement_text: I conjecture that for every class of graphs with polynomial $\omega$-expansion and every integer $\ell\ge1$, there is a constant $m$ (dependent on the class and $\ell$, but not on $|V(G)|$) such that for every graph $G$ in the class and every cost function $q:V(G)\to\mathbb{Q}_{\ge0}$, there actually always exists a balanced separator $C \cup M$ of $G$ with $q(C) \leq q(V(G))/\ell$ for some set $M$ of size at most $m$.
context_text: A balanced separator of $G$ is a set $C\subseteq V(G)$ such that every component of $G-C$ has at most $\frac23|V(G)|$ vertices. For a cost function $q:V(G)\to\mathbb{Q}_{\ge0}$ and $X\subseteq V(G)$, $q(X)=\sum_{x\in X}q(x)$. A model of $K_m$ of depth $d$ is a family of $m$ disjoint vertex sets, each inducing a connected subgraph of radius at most $d$, with an edge between any two of them; $\omega_d(G)$ is the largest $m$ for which $G$ has such a model. A class has polynomial $\omega$-expansion if $\omega_r(G)\le f(r)$ for all $G$ in the class and all $r\ge1$, for some polynomial $f$; by results of Dvořák and Norin and of Plotkin, Rao and Smith, this is equivalent to polynomial expansion and to having strongly sublinear separators (every subgraph $H$ has a balanced separator of order $O(|V(H)|^{1-\varepsilon})$). The author proves a weighted version of the Plotkin–Rao–Smith algorithm: given $G$ with $n$ vertices, $\ell$ and $q$, it finds either a large shallow clique model or disjoint sets $C,M$ with $C\cup M$ a balanced separator, $q(C)\le q(V(G))/\ell$, and $M$ the support of a model of a clique of depth $d=O(\ell\log n)$, so that $|M|\le\omega_d(G)^2d$, which for classes with polynomial $\omega$-expansion is polylogarithmic in $n$. The cost of $M$ cannot be bounded in general: in a star with cost $1/4$ on the centre and $3/4$ spread over the leaves, every balanced separator has cost at least $1/4$. The conjecture is that the dependence of $|M|$ on $n$ can be removed.
notes: Stated as inline prose in the bullet-point remarks following Theorem 5; no labelled theorem environment.
paper_title: On classes of graphs with strongly sublinear separators
